searchText: There are tests that cover the behaviour of the chain in the presence of accounts that have no nonce, no balance, no code, but do have non-zero storage keys. e.g. https://github.com/ethereum/tests/blob/develop/BlockchainTests/GeneralStateTests/stZeroCallsTest/ZeroValue_TransactionCALLwithData_ToOneStorageKey.json These edge cases are a nuisance and such accounts cannot be created on chain that follows any version of the Ethereum protocol except at genesis. I propose we declare the behaviour of the chain undefined in their presence. State Sync #33: - <@!243183686562873344> spurious dragon, fix optimized implementation for TW, diff cleaning - <@!689161464829050960> lots of diff cleaning. Tangerine Whistle and Dao Fork are now merged 🎉 Is there any reason why, in EIP-161, the touched accounts are only deleted at the end of the transaction (as opposed to immediately?) I'm *guessing* the thing mentioned in the rationale, but I'm not sure. For anyone not on the call today (which is most of you), we think it's important to test because before spurious dragon, you could return nothing from initcode but still set storage keys.
